messages:
mina: Heads up — ml-inference-smoke is red on the driver-pin rollout (driver=541.12) on the h200 pool. Failure looks like a kernel launch OOM even for tiny inputs. Job: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/8421 :frowning:
alex: Ugh. Can you paste the failing log snippet? Is it a launch failure or allocation? Could be a driver shim change.
mina: snippet:
```
E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:1234] failed to allocate 65536 bytes: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN: unknown error
E runtime: kernel launch failed: cuLaunchKernel returned CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED
E inference-runner: fatal: persistent memory reserve failed, nvlink status=22
```
alex: nvlink status=22 is weird. I've only seen that with mismatched driver/runtime combos or a new driver gating an ABI change.
ci-bot: [job ml-inference-smoke #8421] re-run suggested by @alex — click to rerun
kevin: Can we rerun on a node with the previous driver (540.33) to see if it's regression? If that reproduces, we can bisect between 540.33 -> 541.12.
sam: I can spin a repro container on my machine with h200 image + 541.12 and try a small workload. @kevin if you trigger the rollback rerun, I'll run an isolated repro and attach traces.
mina: Thanks. @eng-infra (cc @kevin) — can we either rollback the driver on a single canary host or run the CI job against a 540.33 image? If infra prefers, tag `canary-h200-54033` and I'll queue a rerun.
kevin: I'll request a canary image and start the bisect plan. If sam gets a local repro, add `--nvtx` traces and loop a 1-token decode to stress kernel launches.
sam: Will do. If it's reproducible locally I'll paste PERF+nvprof output here. If nobody beats me to it I'll have something within 60m.
mina: Appreciate it. Leaving the CI job open for now — don't merge any driver pins until we confirm. :lock:
